question.text: Per the NISM Series XIX-D workbook (p. 371), the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (DPDPA) and DPDP Rules, 2025 impose obligations on data fiduciaries and data processors. An AIF or Investment Manager that collects and processes investor / LP personal data to deliver fund services is therefore SUBJECT TO which of the following obligations under the Act?

answer.text: None; SEBI-regulated entities are exempt from DPDPA and the DPDP Rules
Only investor-grievance redressal under SEBI circulars; DPDPA is restricted to e-commerce platforms

Obligations applicable to entities handling investor personal data - including obtaining consent, providing notice, applying purpose limitation, implementing reasonable security safeguards and breach reporting under DPDPA / DPDP Rules
Obligations limited to retention of KYC records under PMLA, with no separate DPDPA compliance required

explanation.text: The Logic: Per p. 371 of the workbook, the DPDPA 2023 and DPDP Rules 2025 create obligations on persons handling personal data, and the data-privacy landscape expressly includes AIFs and Investment Managers collecting and processing customer personal data. Option C correctly lists the core DPDPA obligations (consent, notice, purpose limitation, security safeguards, breach reporting) that apply to such entities. The Trap: Option A invents a SEBI-entity exemption; no such exemption exists. Option B falsely restricts DPDPA to e-commerce. Option D collapses DPDPA into PMLA - they are independent obligations that run in parallel. Note: The original stem asked candidates to classify the AIF as a "data fiduciary" vs "data processor", but the checked page does not expressly define "data fiduciary" as "one who determines the purpose and means" or expressly classify an AIF as a fiduciary rather than processor. The stem has been revised to ask about the obligations the Act / Rules impose on AIFs and Investment Managers, which the page does state. Source: 24 NISM-Series-XIX-D Category I and II AIF Managers Certification Examination, January 2026, p. 371.
